title: Fairness at Every Intersection: Uncovering and Mitigating Intersectional Biases in Multimodal Clinical Predictions
abstract: arXiv:2412.00606v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Biases in automated clinical decision-making using Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) impose significant disparities in patient care and treatment outcomes. Conventional approaches have primarily focused on bias mitigation strategies stemming from single attributes, overlooking intersectional subgroups -- groups formed across various demographic intersections (such as race, gender, ethnicity, etc.). Rendering single-attribute mitigation strategies to intersectional subgroups becomes statistically irrelevant due to the varying distribution and bias patterns across these subgroups. translated_title: 每个交叉点的公平性：揭示与缓解多模态临床预测中的交叉性偏见
translated_abstract: 使用电子健康记录（EHR）的自动化临床决策中的偏见会给患者护理和治疗结果带来显著差异。传统方法主要关注基于单一属性的偏见缓解策略，忽视了交叉性亚群体——即由多种人口统计学特征交叉形成的群体（如种族、性别、民族等）。由于这些亚群体之间的数据分布和偏见模式各不相同，将单一属性的缓解策略应用于交叉性亚群体在统计上变得不适用。EHR的多模态特性——包括文本、时间序列、表格、事件和图像等多种来源的数据组合——进一步增加了复杂性，因为对少数群体的影响可能因模态而异。本文迈出了第一步，通过获取大量多模态数据来揭示预测中潜在的交叉性偏见，并提出相应的缓解方法。
tldr: 本文首次系统揭示了电子健康记录多模态临床预测中存在的交叉性偏见问题，指出传统的单一属性偏见缓解策略无法有效应对由多种人口统计学特征交叉形成的亚群体偏见。
en_tdlr: This paper takes the first steps to uncover and mitigate intersectional biases in multimodal clinical predictions from EHR data, demonstrating that conventional single-attribute bias mitigation strategies are insufficient for intersectional subgroups formed across multiple demographic attributes.
